hello.note: Reply: وعليكم السلام (w 'alaikum is-salaam). Casual: هلا (hala) or مرحبا (marhaba).

goodbye.note: Also very Gulf: في أمان الله (fi amaan illah), 'in God's safekeeping'.

please.note: To a woman: من فضلج (min fadhlich). In everyday Gulf requests لو سمحت (law samaht) is more common.

thank_you.note: To a woman: مشكورة (mashkoora). Also: شكرا (shukran), تسلم (tislam).

yes.note: Emiratis also say هيه (heeh). Formal: نعم (na'am).

sorry.note: A woman says: آسفة (aasfa). Very Emirati: السموحة (is-smooha).

excuse_me.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti). Very polite Gulf: طال عمرك (taal 'umrak).

how_are_you.note: To a woman: شحالج؟ (sh-haalich?). Elsewhere in the Gulf: شلونك؟ (shlonak?)

im_fine.note: Lit. 'well, God keep you safe', the usual thanks. To a woman: الله يسلمج (allah ysalmich).

whats_your_name.note: To a woman: شو اسمج؟ (shu ismich?). Extra polite: شو الاسم الكريم؟ (shu il-ism il-kareem?)

where_from.note: To a woman: إنتي من وين؟ (inti min wain?)

speak_english.note: To a woman: تتكلمين إنجليزي؟ (titkallameen ingleezi?)

dont_understand.note: Lit. 'I didn't understand'. Emirati also: مب فاهم (mob faahim); a woman says مب فاهمة (mob faahma).

speak_slowly.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي، تكلمي شوي شوي (law samahti, tkallami shwai shwai).

what.note: Elsewhere in the Gulf: شنو؟ (shinu?) or وش؟ (wish?). Polite 'pardon?': نعم؟ (na'am?)

how_much.note: Often pronounced bcham in the Emirates.

where_bathroom.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti).

can_you_help.note: To a woman: ممكن تساعديني؟ (mumkin tsaa'ideeni?)

water.note: The everyday Gulf word; formal ماء (maa) is understood too.

coffee.note: In the Gulf this usually means Arabic coffee with cardamom, served in small cups.

tea.note: Many Gulf speakers say chaay. Local favourite: كرك (karak), strong spiced milk tea.

bread.note: Careful: عيش ('aish) means rice in the Gulf, not bread.

im_hungry.note: A woman says: أنا جوعانة (ana joo'aana). Many Emiratis say يوعان (yoo'aan).

menu_please.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti).

bill_please.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti).

delicious.note: Also: وايد حلو (waayed hilu), 'really good'. Very Gulf: بنين (bneen).

no_meat.note: Vegetarian: نباتي (nabaati); a woman says نباتية (nabaatiyya).

left.note: To a driver: لف يسار (liff yisaar), 'turn left'.

right.note: To a driver: لف يمين (liff yimeen), 'turn right'.

straight_ahead.note: The everyday Gulf word; you'll also hear على طول ('ala tool).

stop_here.note: To a woman: وقفي هني لو سمحتي (waggfi hni law samahti). Also: نزلني هني (nazzilni hni), 'drop me here'.

hotel.note: The ق is said as g in the Gulf: fundug, not funduq.

train_station.note: In Dubai you'll more often want محطة المترو (mahattat il-metro), the metro station.

want_to_go.note: To a taxi: ودني … (waddni …), 'take me to …'. Elsewhere in the Gulf: أبي / أبغى (abi / abgha).

one_ticket.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti). Also common: تكت (tikit).

too_expensive.note: وايد (waayed), 'very, a lot', is a key Gulf word.

cheaper.note: Plural 'you', addressing the shop, so it suits any assistant.

id_like_this.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti). Also: بآخذ هذا (baakhidh hadha), 'I'll take this'.

just_looking.note: Also: بس أشوف (bas ashoof). Add مشكور (mashkoor) to thank them.

pay_card.note: Shops often ask: كاش ولا كارد؟ (kaash walla kaard?), 'cash or card?'

big.note: Often pronounced chbeer in the Emirates.

tomorrow.note: Also heard: بكرة (bukra), from other Arabic dialects.

yesterday.note: البارحة (il-baarha) is last night, and often just yesterday.

good_night.note: To a woman: تصبحين على خير (tisbaheen 'ala khair). Reply: وإنت من أهله (w inta min ahla).

see_you_later.note: To a woman: أشوفج بعدين (ashoofich ba'dain).

wait_moment.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti). Casual: اصبر شوي (isbir shwai), 'hang on a bit'.

call_police.note: To a woman: اتصلي بالشرطة! (ittasli bish-shurta!). UAE police emergency: 999.

need_doctor.note: A woman says: محتاجة دكتور (mihtaaja diktoor).

im_lost.note: A woman says: أنا ضايعة (ana dhaay'a). Also: ضعت (dhi't), 'I got lost'.

dont_feel_well.note: Also: أنا مريض (ana mareedh), 'I'm ill'; a woman says مريضة (mareedha).

be_careful.note: To a woman: انتبهي! (intibhi!). Also: دير بالك! (deer baalak!)

no_problem.note: Very Gulf: ما عليه (ma 'alaih), 'never mind, it's fine'.

of_course.note: Agreeing to a request, Gulf speakers say أبشر (abshir); to a woman أبشري (abshiri).

dont_know.note: The Gulf way to say it; ما أعرف (ma a'rif) is also used.

dont_like_it.note: مب (mob) is the Emirati 'not'; elsewhere in the Gulf: مو عاجبني (mu 'aajibni).

im_tired.note: A woman says: أنا تعبانة (ana ta'baana). In the Gulf تعبان can also mean unwell.

im_happy.note: A woman says: أنا مستانسة (ana mistaansa). Also: فرحان (farhaan).

welcome.note: To a woman: حياج الله (hayyaach allah). Also: أهلا وسهلا (ahlan wa sahlan).

congratulations.note: Reply: الله يبارك فيك (allah ybaarik feek).

mother.note: My mother: أمي (ummi). Calling her: يمه (yumma). Respectful: الوالدة (il-waalda).

father.note: My father: أبوي (abooy). Calling him: يبه (yuba). Respectful: الوالد (il-waalid).

child.note: Means son (or boy). A daughter: بنت (bint). My children: عيالي ('iyaali).

friend.note: The Gulf word. A female friend: ربيعة (rbee'a). Also: صديق (sadeeg).

this_is_my_friend.note: For a female friend: هذي ربيعتي (hadhi rbee'ti).

are_you_married.note: To a woman: إنتي متزوجة؟ (inti mitzawwja?)

monday.note: From اثنين (ithnain), 'two': the second day of the Arab week.

friday.note: The day of the main weekly prayer, at midday. Many Emiratis say اليمعة (il-yim'a).

sunday.note: From أحد (ahad), 'one': traditionally the first day of the week.

weekend.note: The everyday word. Also: العطلة (il-'utla). In the UAE the weekend is Saturday and Sunday.

what_day.note: Also: أي يوم اليوم؟ (ay yoom il-yoom?)

hundred.note: Arabic digits: ١٠٠. Two hundred: ميتين (meetain). Written formally: مئة.

years_old.note: For 11 and up. From 3 to 10 use سنين (sneen): عمري عشر سنين ('umri 'ashar sneen).

what_colour.note: For a feminine noun: شو لونها؟ (shu loonha?)

another_one.note: Gulf بعد (ba'ad) here means 'more'. To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti).

its_hot.note: Lit. 'the world is heat', the Gulf way to say it. Also: الجو حار (il-jaw haar).

its_raining.note: Rain: مطر (matar). Rare in the Gulf, and usually welcomed.

its_sunny.note: Lit. 'the sun is out'. Also: الجو مشمس (il-jaw mushmis).

its_windy.note: Wind often brings dust: الدنيا غبار (id-dinya ghbaar), 'it's dusty'.

weather_today.note: Elsewhere in the Gulf: شلون الجو اليوم؟ (shlon il-jaw il-yoom?)

beautiful_day.note: Stronger: الجو اليوم روعة (il-jaw il-yoom raw'a), 'the weather's wonderful today'.

umbrella.note: From شمس (shams), 'sun': in the Gulf it's used more for shade than for rain.

summer.note: The fierce peak of summer: القيظ (il-gaidh).

have_reservation.note: Also: أنا حاجز (ana haajiz), 'I've booked'; a woman says حاجزة (haajza).

room.note: At home Gulf speakers also say حجرة (hijra), but for a hotel room it's غرفة.

wifi_password.note: حق (hagg) is the Gulf 'of, belonging to'. Formal: كلمة السر (kilmat is-sirr).

check_out_time.note: Hotels use the English term. Also: متى لازم أطلع؟ (mita laazim atla'?), 'when must I leave?'

map.note: On the phone: طرش لي اللوكيشن (tarrish li il-lokeshan), 'send me the location'.

next_train.note: In Dubai you'll more often ask about المترو (il-metro).

is_this_seat_free.note: Also: في أحد قاعد هني؟ (fee ahad gaa'id hni?), 'is anyone sitting here?'

what_do_you_do.note: To a woman: شو تشتغلين؟ (shu tishtaghleen?)

i_work_in.note: E.g. أشتغل في بنك (ashtaghil fi bank), 'I work in a bank'.

im_student.note: A woman says: أنا طالبة (ana taalba).

meeting.note: I have a meeting: عندي اجتماع ('indi ijtimaa'). Office talk often uses ميتنج (meeting).

im_busy.note: A woman says: أنا مشغولة (ana mashghoola).

day_off.note: Also common: أوف (off), as in اليوم أوف (il-yoom off), 'I'm off today'.

good_job.note: To a woman: عفية عليج! ('afya 'alaich!). Also very Gulf: كفو! (kafu!)

table_for_two.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti).

what_recommend.note: To a woman: شو تنصحيني؟ (shu tinsaheeni?). Also: شو أحسن شي عندكم؟ (shu ahsan shay 'indkum?)

not_spicy.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti). Mildly spicy: شوي حار (shwai haar).

vegetarian_food.note: Asking: عندكم أكل نباتي؟ ('indkum akil nabaati?)

more_water.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti). Also: زيدنا ماي (zeedna maay).

no_sugar.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti). Gulf شكر (shakar) is sugar. A little: شكر خفيف (shakar khafeef).

im_full.note: Usually with الحمد لله (il-hamdu lillah), 'thank God'.

takeaway.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti). You'll be asked: سفري ولا هني؟ (safari walla hni?), 'takeaway or here?'

it_was_delicious.note: To the cook: تسلم إيدك (tislam eedak); to a woman: تسلم إيدج (tislam eedich).

keep_change.note: To a woman: خلي الباقي لج (khalli il-baagi lich).

stomach.note: My stomach hurts: بطني يعورني (batni y'awwirni).

head_hurts.note: Also: عندي صداع ('indi sudaa'), 'I have a headache'.

have_fever.note: Lit. 'I have heat'. Also very Gulf: عندي صخونة ('indi skhoona).

call_ambulance.note: To a woman: اتصلي بالإسعاف! (ittasli bil-is'aaf!). UAE ambulance: 998.

dentist.note: A woman dentist: دكتورة أسنان (diktoora asnaan).

need_rest.note: A woman says: محتاجة أرتاح (mihtaaja artaah). Also: لازم أرتاح (laazim artaah).

feel_better.note: Lit. 'I've got better'. Often with الحمد لله (il-hamdu lillah), 'thank God'.

get_well.note: Also: الله يشفيك (allah yishfeek). Reply: الله يسلمك (allah ysalmak).

lets_meet.note: Also: خلنا نشوف بعض (khallna nshoof ba'adh), 'let's see each other'.

are_you_free.note: To a woman: إنتي فاضية باكر؟ (inti faadhya baachir?)

call_me.note: To a woman: اتصلي علي (ittasli 'alay). Casual: دق علي (dugg 'alay).

your_number.note: To a woman: شو رقم تلفونج؟ (shu ragam tilifoonich?)

see_you_soon.note: To a woman: أشوفج قريب (ashoofich gareeb). Very Gulf: نشوفك على خير (nshoofak 'ala khair).

have_nice_day.note: To a woman: يومج سعيد! (yoomich sa'eed!)

good_luck.note: Also: الله يوفقك (allah ywaffgak); to a woman: الله يوفقج (allah ywaffgich).

happy_birthday.note: Also: كل عام وإنت بخير (kil 'aam w inta bkhair), said for Eid too.

thanks_a_lot.note: Lit. 'you didn't fall short'. To a woman: مشكورة، ما قصرتي (mashkoora, ma gassarti).

miss_you.note: To a woman: اشتقت لج (ishtagt lich). Very Gulf: فقدتك (fagadtak).
